answer: Churn is counted in walnut, and copper publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 18% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the wander history. A 373 account operation therefore ties up 2 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
